final_message:
All 10 tests pass. I'm leaving the work uncommitted since you didn't ask for a commit.

The renderer is implemented in `src/lexer.ts`, `src/lookup.ts` and `src/render.ts`, and `node --test` passes all 10 tests.

- **`lookup`** walks the dotted path and only reads own properties, so `constructor` and `__proto__` come back `undefined`.
- **`isTruthy`** uses JavaScript truthiness, with an empty array as the one exception.
- **`tokenize`** splits text from `{{ }}`, `{{{ }}}`, `{{#if}}`, `{{else}}` and `{{/if}}` tags, and throws `unterminated tag` when a tag never closes.
- **`render`** tracks `{{#if}}` blocks with a stack, so it throws `unexpected {{else}}`, `unexpected {{/if}}` or `unclosed {{#if}}` as the README specifies. Filters apply left to right, and `default`, `upper` and `lower` are supported.

Two choices the README didn't settle:
- Filters are evaluated even inside a false `{{#if}}` branch, so an unknown filter throws regardless of the data.
- `{{ items.length }}` returns the array length, because `length` is an own property of arrays. Strings are not looked into, as the README says.

Unspecified inputs such as a bare `{{#if}}` with no path currently render as empty rather than throwing. Say if you'd rather they throw.
